papers.title: From detection to decision: molecular, genomic, and AI innovations for managing Ganoderma boninense in oil palm.
papers.abstract: Ganoderma boninense causes basal stem rot (BSR) in oil palm, resulting in substantial economic losses, particularly for smallholders who contribute approximately 40% of global production. This review synthesizes advances in molecular diagnostic techniques (qPCR, LAMP), whole-genome sequencing of resistant Elaeis guineensis genotypes, and AI-driven remote sensing to enhance understanding of G. boninense pathobiology. Soilborne mycelia of the pathogen can persist for more than 10 y. Asymptomatic infections, which are frequently missed by conventional methods, can lead to significant disease spread within plantations over 2 y. CRISPR-based paper-strip tests have demonstrated high sensitivity (detecting < 1 pg DNA in laboratory settings), while marker-assisted selection has helped identify additional resistance QTLs. Trichoderma biofilms and biodegradable fumigants reduced soil inoculum by 50-75% in controlled studies. AI-based decision support systems have demonstrated promising accuracy for guiding interventions and potential cost savings, although further field validation across diverse conditions is needed.

papers.title: Pantoea Species Isolated from Onion Plants and Bulbs Across Different Regions of Chile.
papers.abstract: Onions are one of the main vegetables cultivated in Chile. In recent years, changing climate conditions have favored the emergence of new bacterial diseases, where Pantoea species have been reported as causal agents of onion leaf blight and bulb rot in central Chile. The objective of this work was to study the abundance of Pantoea spp. isolated from symptomatic onion plants sampled in different regions of Chile. The identification of Pantoea species was determined based on gyrB, leuS and rpoB genes sequences, revealing Pantoea agglomerans as the most frequently isolated species, followed by Pantoea ananatis and Pantoea eucalypti . Pathogenicity tests were performed. Only three of the 20 isolated strains showed clear symptoms of bulb damage, with P. ananatis exhibiting the most severe symptoms. The complete genome of a pathogenic strain of each identified species was sequenced. These genomes were used for the implementation of PCR-High Resolution Melting-based system determining characteristic profiles of each species in order to facilitate the identification of the isolates in onion samples. Six primer pairs of housekeeping genes previously used in multilocus analysis were used to test their ability to differentiate between Pantoea species. The primer pairs gyrB and leuS showed the greatest discrimination among the Pantoea species. In this study, the identification of Pantoea species isolated from onion crops in Chile, revealed that only a small proportion were pathogenic, even in diseased plants. This highlights complex plant-bacteria interactions and suggests PCR-HRM as a useful tool to study these populations and better understand disease development.

papers.title: Population Genomics and Virulence Analyses Reveal Migration Pathways of Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici Between Southeastern Tibet and Sichuan.
papers.abstract: Wheat stripe rust, caused by Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici ( Pst ), is one of the most damaging diseases of wheat in China. Southeastern Tibet has recently been identified as an important source of Pst inoculum; however, the population genetic relationships and dispersal pathways connecting this region to Sichuan remain unclear. In this study, 220 Pst isolates collected from southeastern Tibet and Sichuan in 2025 were characterized using 19 Chinese differentials, 18 Yr single-gene differentials, and a 5K genotyping-by-target sequencing platform to assess virulence diversity, population structure, and potential migration pathways. Virulence analyses identified 66 previously described and 76 additional races using the Chinese differentials, while 148 races were distinguished using the Yr single-gene differentials. None of the isolates exhibited virulence against Yr5 or Yr15 . Population genetic analyses revealed that the Qamdo (CD) population in eastern Tibet exhibited the highest genetic diversity and substantial admixture. Strong genetic connectivity between Qamdo and populations in southeastern Tibet and Sichuan suggested extensive regional gene flow. Close genetic relationships between Qamdo and populations from Garzê (SCGZ), Jiangyou (SCJY), and Guangyuan (SCGY) further indicated that Qamdo may serve as a bridge for pathogen dispersal. These findings support the potential contribution of oversummering Pst populations in southeastern Tibet to inoculum sources in Sichuan and highlight the epidemiological significance of the Nyingchi-Qamdo-Sichuan corridor. This study provides insights into regional Pst migration and informs resistance breeding and stripe rust management strategies.

papers.title: Rat hepatitis E virus RNA detection in isolated cases of acute undifferentiated febrile illness without acute hepatitis.
papers.abstract: Rat hepatitis E virus (ratHEV; Rocahepevirus ratti) is an emerging zoonotic pathogen whose clinical spectrum is predominantly hepatic. Whether ratHEV causes acute undifferentiated febrile illness (AUFI) without acute hepatitis has not been systematically evaluated. This retrospective observational study at a southern Spain tertiary hospital (April 2021-October 2023) evaluated patients tested for Rickettsia spp. and/or Coxiella burnetii. AUFI was defined as community-acquired fever ≥38°C lasting <21 days without localizing features or initial etiology; patients with acute hepatitis were excluded. AUFI cases were compared with contemporaneous febrile patients presenting with a localizing focus. The primary outcome was sequence-confirmed infection. Detections without sequence recovery were classified as probable infections. Of 1,684 patients assessed, 312 were eligible: 81 with AUFI (median age 53 years [IQR, 37-64]; 54 [66.7%] men) and 231 comparators. Sequence-confirmed ratHEV infection occurred in 1/81 AUFI patients (1.2%; 95% CI, 0.2-6.7) and 0/231 comparators (0%; 95% CI, 0-1.6; P = 0.260). Two additional AUFI patients had detectable ratHEV RNA without sequence recovery. Combining confirmed and probable infections, ratHEV RNA was detected in 3/81 AUFI patients (3.7%; 95% CI, 1.3-10.3; P = 0.017). The confirmed infection presented as a self-limiting febrile illness without liver dysfunction, ratHEV RNA cleared upon fever resolution. The recovered genotype C1 sequence clustered with ratHEV rodent sequences from the same region. RatHEV RNA was detected exclusively among AUFI patients. These findings support prospectively evaluating ratHEV as a potential cause of AUFI where the virus circulates in animal reservoirs.

papers.title: Rapid and sensitive on-site detection of PBoV G3 using an EsCas13d-based platform.
papers.abstract: Rapid, sensitive, and user-friendly nucleic acid diagnostic methods are crucial for controlling the spread of PBoV G3. In this study, we developed SENTRY (Single-step Enzymatic Nucleic acid Targeted Reporter Yield), a pathogen detection platform designed for on-site deployment in resource-limited settings. Combined with GENE (General Extraction-free Nucleic acid Exposure reagent), a room-temperature lysis protocol, SENTRY can release viral nucleic acids within 5 min. The addition of accessory proteins enhances the sensitivity of the one-step SENTRY platform and shortens the reaction time. SENTRY provides results within 30 min, with clinical sample detection rates matching those of qPCR, and shows no cross-reactivity with non-target viruses. The system operates efficiently at body temperature (∼37 °C) without requiring temperature control devices. Lyophilized reagents make SENTRY robust to transport conditions and extend shelf life. Overall, these features make SENTRY highly suitable for POCT outside conventional laboratory environments.

papers.title: Conventional and inverted SERS configurations in pathogen diagnostics on the basis of plasmonic gold nanostars ink.
papers.abstract: Conventional surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) methodologies typically depend on prefabricated substrates, which can constrain their utility for rapid, in-situ diagnostics. While nano-inks offer a route toward flexible sensing, their application typically still follows a direct, substrate-based paradigm. Trends toward the miniaturization of Raman spectroscopy and on-site diagnostics necessitate a fundamental rethinking of sensor design, prioritizing minimal sample preparation and direct analysis. Gold nanostar (AuNSs)-based plasmonic ink is presented as a versatile platform for surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS)-based detection of pyocyanin - a key virulence factor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Two SERS configurations are explored: a conventional paper-based sensor, used to establish the analytical performance of the AuNSs ink (LOD 15 nM in saliva), and an inverted approach, where the ink is deposited directly onto a medical cotton swab pre-loaded with the sample. The inverted configuration, coupled with a portable Raman spectrometer (785 nm), enables direct, substrate-free detection of pyocyanin with a clinically relevant LOD of 5 μM and requires minimal sample pretreatment. Spike-and-recovery experiments in saliva yielded recoveries of 96-105% (s r ≤ 0.10), confirming the accuracy of the method. The inverted SERS approach on cotton swabs thus offers a practical, rapid, and simple route for point-of-care screening of P. aeruginosa infections, circumventing the need for prefabricated sensors or laboratory equipment. By transforming the standard clinical swab into an active SERS substrate, the inverted approach provides a practical, substrate-free, and equipment-light platform for direct pathogen screening at the patient's bedside. This strategy addresses key barriers to SERS implementation - reliance on prefabricated sensors, complex sample handling, and bulky instrumentation - offering a realistic and scalable solution for non-invasive screening. This approach is particularly significant for the analysis of potentially bio-contaminated surfaces, such as medical instruments or hospital environments, where direct contact with the analyte is hazardous or undesirable.

papers.title: Multimodal AI in Oral Cancer: A PRISMA-Guided Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Oral cancer presents significant diagnostic and prognostic challenges, often due to late-stage detection and tumour heterogeneity. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML), offer promising solutions by integrating multimodal biomedical data. This PRISMA-guided systematic review evaluates over 82 studies from 2015 to 2025 that apply convolutional neural networks, transformers and graph neural networks to oral cancer, using combinations of histopathology, radiology, genomics and clinical data. Results indicate that multimodal AI models consistently outperform unimodal approaches in diagnostic accuracy, AUC and survival prediction. Architectures employing attention mechanisms, graph embedding and fusion transformers demonstrate superior performance in tasks such as early lesion detection and treatment outcome modelling. Despite these advances, challenges persist in generalisability, data standardisation and clinical validation. Multimodal AI thus represents a paradigm shift toward precision oncology in oral cancer, warranting further research focused on interpretability, prospective validation and ethical clinical deployment.

papers.title: A chromosome-level genome of the king penguin (Aptenodytes patagonicus): a resource for linking genotype to fitness in a long-lived vertebrate.
papers.abstract: The king penguin (Aptenodytes patagonicus) is a long-lived seabird of the Southern Ocean that is emerging as a promising model in the wild for studying evolution. We present a high-quality, haplotype-resolved 1.35 Gb chromosome-level genome of an adult female king penguin - 'Pen/Se-guin' - assembled using PacBio HiFi long-reads and Hi-C proximity data. A total of 95% of the assembly is assigned to 34 chromosomes (32 autosomes, plus the Z and W chromosomes). The primary haplotype has a BUSCO completeness of 97.2%, and across both haplotypes the assembly has a k-mer completeness of 99.7% and a quality value of 63.8. We also assembled a circularised mitogenome (20,520 bp) containing the avian tandem duplication. Repetitive sequence annotation showed that 16.3% of the genome comprises repetitive elements, with LINEs representing the most abundant transposable element class (5.6%). Gene prediction using an extensive multi-tissue RNA-seq dataset resulted in 18,081 predicted protein-coding genes, of which 17,081 were functionally annotated, with a BUSCO completeness of 98.4% and an OMArk completeness of 97.3%. Compared with the previous draft genome, the presented genome shows a 30-fold increase in assembly contiguity and a substantially improved genome annotation, exceeding the standards of the Earth BioGenome Project and Vertebrate Genomes Project. This genome provides a foundation for ongoing and future studies using the king penguin to investigate genotype-fitness relationships, ageing, life-history evolution, and adaptation.

papers.title: Multi-omics data integration in bioinformatics: methods, applications, and the path toward biological reasoning.
papers.abstract: High-throughput technologies now make it possible to simultaneously generate genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data. Spatial and single-cell platforms, in turn, provide cellular and spatial information in greater detail. Relying on a single omics method captures only a fraction of this complexity and often overlooks interactions across different layers. Despite these advances, clinical applications remain limited. This review examines integration strategies, along with their applications in various diseases, and the machine learning methods used to implement them. Rather than focusing solely on predictive performance, the aim is to support biological reasoning by formulating testable hypotheses, drawing causal inferences, and gaining insights that can guide clinical decisions. A reanalysis of a publicly available chronic lymphocytic leukemia dataset revealed that one data type was missing in approximately one-third of patients. When early and intermediate integration were combined with simple zero imputation, agreement dropped to chance and near-chance levels. In contrast, late integration, which does not require data imputation, was largely unaffected by this issue. This demonstrates that findings regarding integration strategies cannot be considered in isolation from how missing data are handled. The review also covers approaches that directly address missing data. Major barriers to clinical application include confounding batch effects, unreliable feature attribution when features are correlated, and deficiencies in clinical quality assurance. This review proposes four criteria to help identify models that not only ensure statistical validity but also genuinely support biological reasoning: mechanistic specificity, causal grounding, failure transparency, and decision relevance.

papers.title: The Journey from Podium to Paper: Examining the Publication Rate of High-Quality Genetics and Genomics Research.
papers.abstract: Publication success of conference presentations varies across medical specialties. Despite their importance in academic medicine, many studies presented at scientific meetings are not submitted or accepted for peer-reviewed literature. We investigated the publication rate of platform presentations at the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) Annual Clinical Genetics Meetings (2017-2020) and identified factors associated with successful publication. All platform presentations from ACMG Annual Meetings (2017-2020) were reviewed. Publications were identified using PubMed and Google Scholar using abstract titles, keywords, and author names. Study characteristics were compared between published and unpublished abstracts using chi-squared and Mann-Whitney tests. Of 3,566 submitted abstracts, 209 (5.9%) were selected as platform presentations. The overall publication rate was 62.7% (131/209) with a median time to publication of 2 years. Published studies were more likely to be multicenter (52.7% vs 20.5%, p=0.01), externally funded (86.3% vs 24.4%, p=0.01), and have statistically significant primary outcomes (96.7% vs 68.8%, p=0.01) compared to unpublished studies. One-third of publications appeared in Genetics in Medicine (32%). Nearly two-thirds of ACMG platform presentations (2017-2020) achieved peer-reviewed publication within 5 years. Multicenter collaboration, external funding, and statistically significant outcomes are associated with higher publication rates.

papers.title: In Vivo CRISPR Base Editing of ANGPTL3 for Durable Lipid Lowering.
papers.abstract: Circulating concentrations of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins are leading risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease 1 . Despite several approved lipid-lowering medications, most patients fail to achieve target lipid levels under the chronic care treatment model 2,3 . Here, we describe a potential single-course treatment in which an infusion of guide RNA and mRNA encoding a CRISPR adenine base editor-encapsulated within a GalNAc-lipid nanoparticle-leads to durable, liver-selective inactivation of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a known driver of increased LDL-C and triglyceride concentrations. Analyses in human liver cells in vitro confirmed that the base editor introduces a DNA base-pair change at the target ANGPTL3 locus with no detectable off-target editing at any of approximately 3000 candidate sites or treatment-related structural variants. Targeted ANGPTL3 inactivation in nonhuman primates was well-tolerated and led to a > 90% mean reduction in circulating ANGPTL3 protein, with durability confirmed out to 3 years following a single dose. In mouse and nonhuman primate models of hyperlipidemia, gene inactivation was associated with reductions of approximately 40 to 50% in LDL-C and 50 to 70% in triglycerides. These results provided the scientific foundation for initiation of an ongoing first-in-human clinical trial in patients with refractory hyperlipidemia syndromes.

papers.title: Perspective. Precision Nutrition at a Crossroads: From Biological Prediction to Contextual Implementation.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrition has substantially reshaped nutritional science by demonstrating that individuals can respond differently to identical dietary exposures. Advances in genomics, metabolomics, proteomics, microbiome research, wearable technologies, digital health, and artificial intelligence have improved our ability to characterize biological heterogeneity and predict individual responses to diet. However, demonstrating such variability does not necessarily result in nutritional strategies that provide clinically meaningful benefits beyond established evidence-based care. A critical distinction should therefore be made between precision nutrition as a discovery science, which has convincingly established interindividual heterogeneity in dietary responses, and precision nutrition as an intervention science, which must demonstrate meaningful incremental value over dietary approaches already supported by clinical evidence. Despite increasingly sophisticated technologies and predictive models, evidence of consistent improvements in long-term health outcomes, cost-effectiveness, scalability, and equity remains limited. In this Perspective, we argue that precision nutrition has reached a critical crossroads. We distinguish prediction of individual responses, which is only one route to precision nutrition, from treatment-effect heterogeneity, treatment selection and clinical utility. We then propose contextual precision nutrition as a translational framework that integrates biological responsiveness with the behavioral, psychological, social, cultural, economic, and environmental determinants of dietary behavior. Rather than claiming novelty for these components, the framework integrates them into a decision logic that asks whether biological information improves the selection of a dietary strategy beyond routine information and established care, and how that strategy can be delivered and sustained. It complements population-based dietary recommendations by refining their implementation and maximizing adherence and real-world effectiveness. Ultimately, the success of precision nutrition will be determined not by the sophistication of its predictions but by its ability to translate biological knowledge into interventions that are clinically effective, scalable, equitable, and sustainable, thereby improving both individual and population health.

papers.title: Microenvironment of Bone and Joint Infection: Examining the Microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a major complication of arthroplasty, and conventional diagnostic methods for PJI remain limited by suboptimal sensitivity, long turnaround times, high cost, and patient inconvenience, particularly in biofilm-associated and culture-negative infections. Emerging data suggest that the infected joint microenvironment contains host- and pathogen-derived molecular signatures with substantial diagnostic potential. This review evaluates current evidence on microenvironment-related biomarkers in PJI, including host extracellular vesicles, host cell-free nucleic acids (microRNA/cell-free DNA), non-host-derived biomarkers, and sequencing-based pathogen detection techniques. Host-derived biomarkers show favorable discriminatory capability by characterizing inflammatory and immune responses, and metagenomic and sequencing-based technologies improve pathogen identification. Despite encouraging diagnostic performance, widespread clinical implementation remains limited due to a lack of standardization, cost, and limited prospective validation. Future prospective multicenter studies should integrate conventional microbiological methods with molecular and microenvironment-based approaches to improve diagnostic accuracy.

papers.title: Routine urinalysis-based machine learning framework for predicting urine culture contamination.
papers.abstract: Urine culture contamination is a common preanalytical challenge, yet conventional urinalysis strategies rarely treat it as an independent outcome. This retrospective study included 8446 specimens from 6686 patients, split at the patient level into training and internal validation sets. An additional 3481 specimens from 2819 patients at two other campuses of the same hospital system were used for external validation. Nineteen demographic and routine urinalysis variables were analyzed. We developed a two-stage XGBoost framework that first distinguished bacterial growth from negative culture and then contamination from pathogenic growth. Thresholds were selected during training to maintain ≥95% sensitivity for bacterial-growth detection in Stage 1 and ≥ 95% specificity for pathogenic growth in Stage 2. Comparators included one-stage three-class, class-weighted, and binary contamination-versus-rest XGBoost models and SEC-based rules. The binary contamination-versus-rest model and SEC-based rules showed limited contamination recall (0.411 [0.348-0.475] to 0.589 [0.525-0.651]). Relative to the two-stage reference, the one-stage three-class model had significantly lower contamination recall (0.572 versus 0.732) and pathogenic-growth recall (0.746 versus 0.901) in internal validation (both Holm-adjusted P < 0.001), whereas the class-weighted model achieved comparable contamination recall (0.765) but with reduced pathogenic-growth recall (0.741) and a higher pathogen-to-contamination error rate (0.091 versus 0.033). Decision curve analysis showed positive net benefit at both external sites. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified bacilli count, SEC, and WBC as the main contributors in Stage 2. This two-stage framework may support urine culture diagnostic stewardship by flagging approximately three-quarters of contaminated cultures before culture reporting. Prospective multicenter and cross-platform validation is needed before routine implementation.

papers.title: Evaluation of targets for normalization of viral pathogen concentrations in building dust.
papers.abstract: Building dust is potentially an important public health tool for monitoring human pathogens because it contains genetic material from pathogens. However, building dust is heterogeneous and presents technical challenges for environmental pathogen surveillance. To effectively use pathogen measurements in building dust for environmental surveillance, normalization procedures that account for human contribution to dust may be necessary and could help account for variability in occupancy and temporal resolution. Our analysis investigates potential indicators of human emission that could be used to normalize data on concentration of pathogens in dust. Ninety-nine vacuum dust samples were collected from 33 buildings and concentrations were measured for three emission indicators ( i.e. , human cytochrome B gene, Carjivirus communis (previously crAssphage), and pepper mild mottle virus) and two respiratory pathogens ( i.e. SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus). All of these were detected in ≥91% of the samples, with the exception of influenza A virus (73%). Most pairings of indicators (nine of 10) showed a weak to moderate positive correlation with one another (Kendall's τ ≤ 0.28). Correlations between occupancy and emission indicators and respiratory pathogens were weak (Kendall's τ < |0.15|) and non-significant ( p > 0.1). Among all potential markers, MT-CYB was most promising, with detection in 96% of the samples, higher concentration than others, and stronger correlation with other potential measures of occupancy.

papers.title: Genomic Profiling of the Virulence Potential and Antimicrobial Resistance of Shiga Toxin-Producing Escherichia coli from Surface Water and Animal Sources.
papers.abstract: The aim of this work was to characterize the pathogenic potential of Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) circulating in environmental and animal reservoirs. To achieve this, 225 genomes were analyzed: four genomes were obtained from bovine mastitis isolates, and 221 were obtained from the NCBI Pathogen Detection database originating from surface water and animal fecal samples. All genomes were analyzed to identify virulence-associated factors and antimicrobial resistance profiles in strains collected from surface water and animal samples. Virulence analysis revealed that stx1 and stx2 were detected in 32% and 44% of isolates, respectively. Environmental genomes frequently carried adhesion and LEE-associated genes, while mastitis isolates lacked these markers but exhibited enriched iron uptake systems and hemolysins, indicating niche-specific virulence repertoires. Resistance analysis identified 105 genes that contribute to antimicrobial resistance against multiple antibiotic families, including beta-lactams, quinolones, tetracyclines, aminoglycosides, and polymyxins. Phylogenetic analysis classified the strains mainly into phylogroups B1 (63.56%) and E (28%), and serotyping identified 41 serotypes, with O157:H7 being the most common (25.33%). MLST revealed 46 STs, with ST11 being the predominant one in animal fecal isolates. Overall, the data indicate a genetically diverse STEC population, with shared lineages among water, feces, and mastitis, as well as combined virulence and multidrug resistance profiles. This supports the need to incorporate genomic surveillance in environmental and livestock reservoirs to anticipate and mitigate the risks of transmission to the human population.

papers.title: Single-Nucleus Transcriptomics Reveals Cell Type Specific Defence Responses and Identifies AhWRKY40 as a Key Regulator of Peanut Resistance to Sclerotium rolfsii.
papers.abstract: Peanut stem rot caused by Sclerotium rolfsii is a devastating soil borne disease that severely constrains peanut production worldwide. Despite its economic importance, highly resistant peanut cultivars are still largely unavailable, and the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying peanut resistance remain poorly understood. We obtained a total of 29,308 high-quality nuclei, annotated five major cell types, and detected 52,819 expressed genes. Comparative analysis revealed widespread transcriptional reprogramming and a predominance of downregulated genes in response to pathogen infection, accompanied by a substantial reduction in cell abundance across all cell populations. Notably, epidermal cells harboured the highest proportion of disease resistance genes. Pseudotime trajectory analysis further demonstrated that S. rolfsii infection altered cellular transcriptional states and induced cell type specific immune reprogramming. Integrative analyses combining gene coexpression, pseudotime dynamics, virtual knockout, and transgenic validation consistently identified AhWRKY40 as a key regulatory factor associated with disease resistance. Overexpression of AhWRKY40 enhanced resistance to S. rolfsii and was accompanied by increased accumulation of jasmonic acid (JA) and salicylic acid (SA), suggesting its involvement in hormone-mediated defence responses. Collectively, our study provides new insights into the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying peanut resistance to stem rot, identifies AhWRKY40 as a promising candidate gene for disease resistance, and establishes a valuable resource for functional genomics and molecular breeding to improve southern blight resistance in peanut.

papers.title: Off-panel resistance determinants in a high-resistance setting: comparative evaluation of syndromic multiplex PCR, metagenomic sequencing, and phenotypic AST in bloodstream infections.
papers.abstract: Rapid syndromic molecular panels substantially reduce turnaround time for bloodstream infection diagnosis by identifying common pathogens and selected antimicrobial resistance determinants directly from positive blood cultures. However, their fixed target repertoires may limit diagnostic coverage in settings with diverse endemic resistance mechanisms and clinically relevant off-panel organisms. This retrospective comparative diagnostic study evaluated direct-from-positive-blood-culture metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), the BioFire Blood Culture Identification 2 (BCID2) panel, and routine microbiological methods across 165 positive blood-culture episodes from 145 patients at a tertiary-care center with a high burden of antimicrobial resistance. Complete recovery of the routine-culture organism set was achieved in 155/165 episodes (93.9%) by mNGS and 142/165 (86.1%) by BCID2. Among 23 episodes with incomplete routine-set recovery by BCID2, mNGS restored complete coverage in 18 (78.3%). For meropenem resistance, sensitivity was numerically higher with mNGS than with BCID2 (90.0% versus 75.0%), whereas ceftriaxone-resistance sensitivity among Enterobacterales was numerically higher with BCID2 (97.5% versus 85.0%); neither paired difference was statistically significant. BCID2 meropenem very major errors were concentrated among non-fermenting gram-negative organisms, particularly Acinetobacter baumannii , and were frequently associated with off-panel bla OXA-23 detected by mNGS. Overall, targeted syndromic testing and mNGS demonstrated complementary diagnostic performance, with mNGS extending organism and resistance-mechanism coverage beyond predefined molecular targets, while phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing remained necessary for definitive susceptibility assessment.IMPORTANCERapid molecular blood-culture panels provide clinically actionable results, but are inherently restricted to predefined pathogen and resistance targets. This limitation is particularly relevant in regions where local antimicrobial resistance epidemiology includes mechanisms not represented within commercial panel repertoires. In this study, metagenomic sequencing improved recovery of routine-culture organisms and identified off-panel carbapenem resistance determinants underlying several false-susceptible panel results, particularly OXA-23 in Acinetobacter baumannii . However, broader genomic detection did not consistently improve phenotypic resistance prediction across antimicrobial classes. These findings illustrate that diagnostic breadth and phenotypic predictive accuracy are distinct attributes and support the use of metagenomic sequencing as a complementary approach to rapid targeted testing and conventional antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

papers.title: From Genomics to Diagnostics: Combating the Spread of Vascular Streak Dieback in North America.
papers.abstract: Vascular streak dieback (VSD) has emerged as a major threat to woody ornamental production in the United States (U.S.), currently affecting at least 50 tree and shrub species across 25 botanical genera in at least twelve U.S. states. The putative causal agent, here termed the VSD-associated Ceratobasidiaceae lineage (Csp), presents diagnostic challenges due to its fastidious growth requirements and vascular colonization pattern. Here, we integrate genomics-guided marker discovery with multi-platform genome-anchored tools (SSR, TaqMan qPCR, and LAMP that target unique genomic regions identified through comparative genomics) to deliver a field-deployable, genome-anchored toolkit for detection and genotyping of Csp across nurseries and landscapes. We evaluated the performance of these tools using 103 samples representing DNA isolated from 64 VSD-symptomatic plants or their fungal isolates and 39 non-target Ceratobasidiaceae outgroups. Genome assembly of Illumina reads yielded ten informative microsatellite markers with an overall amplification success rate of 95.8% (91.7%-100.0% across Csp samples). These markers demonstrated strong performance in distinguishing the Csp samples from the outgroups. Among the three TaqMan probes developed, VSD048 exhibited superior performance with 100% detection across Csp samples, characterized by cycle threshold (C T ) values of 26.8 ± 4.2, and no cross-reactivity with C. theobromae or other Ceratobasidiaceae species. A multi-laboratory ring trial confirmed the reproducibility of the VSD048 TaqMan assay across various testing platforms. The loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay targeting the Csp-unique region achieved a sensitivity of 0.82 [95% CI 0.68-0.968] and specificity of 1.00 [95% CI 1.00-1.00], with a practical detection threshold of approximately 25 copies of the target region. Our molecular survey of the disease revealed a surprisingly broad host range beyond Cercis canadensis (Eastern redbud), encompassing eight additional genera, and confirmed its geographical distribution across the eastern and midwestern U.S. These validated molecular tools provide rapid, sensitive, and specific detection methods for Csp surveillance and management. The field-applicable LAMP assay and laboratory-based TaqMan/SSR protocols offer complementary approaches for different diagnostic scenarios, thereby enabling early detection and supporting efforts to limit the spread of this emerging pathogen in nursery and landscape settings.

papers.title: How Stroke Genetics Is Impacting Clinical Care: Now and the Future.
papers.abstract: The past decade has seen a transformation in our understanding of the genetics of stroke. However, a commonly asked question is how do these advances impact the practicing clinician now, and what are their implications for clinical care in the future? This review outlines the major recent advances in stroke genetics and addresses 4 questions most relevant to the clinician: What do we now know about the genetic architecture of stroke? When and how should genetic testing be used to identify monogenic stroke? How can genetic information be applied to risk stratification and prevention? And what therapeutic implications are emerging from genetic discoveries? It highlights the success of genome-wide association studies in stroke and how these have transformed how we understand the genetic architecture of stroke. An increasing number of monogenic forms of cerebral small vessel disease are being identified, and guidance on when and how to test for them is covered. Polygenic risk scores are gaining increasing attention. How these can be applied, and the challenges in their use are discussed. Lastly, the impact of genomics on stroke therapeutics, whether by identifying new targets, assessing causality using techniques such as Mendelian randomization, or pharmacogenomics, is discussed.

papers.title: An Enzyme-Mediated Duplex Exponential Amplification Assay for Rapid Detection of Plasmodiophora brassicae .
papers.abstract: Clubroot, caused by the soilborne obligate biotrophic protist Plasmodiophora brassicae , substantially reduces the yield and quality of cruciferous crops worldwide. In this study, an enzyme-mediated duplex exponential amplification (EmDEA) assay was developed for rapid detection of P. brassicae in extracted DNA. By comparing the P. brassicae strain 3A genome with representative bacterial, fungal, and oomycete genome assemblies, we identified 157 candidate regions that showed no detectable matches in the selected non-target genomes under the specified alignment criteria. Pbspec1, a fragment within the annotated locus PBTT_08698, was selected based on computational non-target screening, within-species conservation, and suitability for assay design. PCR amplification and Sanger sequencing were used to validate the target fragment. Six forward primers, six reverse primers, and six RNA probes were screened, and F2-R4-RNA2 was selected for subsequent EmDEA experiments. Using serial dilutions of purified recombinant plasmid DNA, the F2-R4-RNA2 combination consistently detected template concentrations of 1.0 × 10 3 copies/μL and above. No amplification was observed from the 12 non-target fungal or bacterial organisms. The assay detected P. brassicae in DNA extracted from four infected root samples and three naturally infested soil samples. All tested positive samples produced detectable fluorescence during a programmed 20-min run on a portable isothermal fluorescence instrument. These results support the potential use of EmDEA for rapid preliminary screening of P. brassicae following DNA extraction.

papers.title: Evaluation of ITS copy number variation among Clarireedia jacksonii isolates using single-copy genetic markers cam and hsp60 .
papers.abstract: Molecular tools are widely used for plant pathogen detection and quantification. Recent quantitative PCR applications for the turfgrass disease causal agent Clarireedia jacksonii were developed targeting the ITS region and showed potential utility in improved disease management. However, accurate and consistent pathogen quantification is contingent on stable copy numbers of the target genes across populations. In this study, we evaluated the genomic copy number of molecular markers in C. jacksonii using in silico analyses, quantitative PCR, and digital PCR. Calmodulin ( cam ), elongation factor 1-alpha ( ef1α ), and minichromosome maintenance protein 7 ( mcm7 ) were consistently identified as single-copy loci, whereas ITS exhibited multiple copies in two out of nine assemblies. Digital PCR confirmed that cam and heat shock protein 60 ( hsp60 ) closely followed theoretical single-copy expectations across a genomic DNA dilution series of C. jacksonii isolate HRS10. In the analysis of 27 C. jacksonii isolates, ITS was consistently detected as a multicopy locus, with copy number estimates ranging from 33 to 48 copies per genome when normalized using cam and from 34 to 52 copies per genome when normalized using hsp60 . These results demonstrate that ITS copy number variation among C. jacksonii isolates was consistently observed, independent of the single-copy reference locus used for normalization. Therefore, single-copy genetic markers, such as cam and hsp60 , may represent superior choices for accurate and stable estimation of fungal genome equivalents in C. jacksonii .

papers.title: Molecular detection of Coxiella burnetii and a Coxiellaceae bacterium in Hyalomma asiaticum and Dermacentor nuttalli ticks collected in Mongolia.
papers.abstract: Coxiella burnetii, the causative agent of Q fever, is a zoonotic pathogen for which epidemiological data are limited in Mongolia. This study investigated the presence of C. burnetii in ticks collected across Mongolia from forest, pasture, and livestock-associated environments. A total of 7,511 ticks were collected from 42 Soums across 12 provinces and 2 districts of Ulaanbaatar between May and June 2018. Molecular detection of Coxiella-related organisms was performed using 46 DNA samples, comprising 28 individual-tick samples and 18 pooled-tick samples representing 489 ticks, by nested PCR targeting IS1111 and the 16S rRNA gene. Twenty DNA samples (2 individual ticks and 18 pools) were PCR-positive. Sequencing and phylogenetic analysis revealed that 9 Hyalomma asiaticum tick pools contained 16S rRNA sequences of C. burnetii, whereas 11 Dermacentor nuttalli samples (2 individual ticks and 9 pools) contained 16S rRNA sequences of a Coxiellaceae bacterium. Two individual D. nuttalli ticks yielded IS1111 sequences closely related to C. burnetii, whereas the corresponding 16S rRNA sequences clustered with a Coxiellaceae bacterium, highlighting discordance between the 2 molecular targets. The C. burnetii sequences detected in H. asiaticum were closely related to clade A strains reported from the United States, Japan, Greenland, and Korea, whereas sequences detected in D. nuttalli clustered with Coxiella endosymbiont sequences. This study provides molecular evidence for the presence of C. burnetii in H. asiaticum tick pools in Mongolia and demonstrates that Mongolian ticks harbor genetically diverse Coxiella-related bacteria, highlighting the need for further investigation of their epidemiological significance.

papers.title: Educational framework to strengthen the variant scientist workforce in clinical genomics.
papers.abstract: The integration of genomics into clinical care has created an urgent need for accurate, standardized variant interpretation. Variant Scientists (VSs) play a central role in translating sequencing results into clinically actionable findings, yet formal education and standardized training pathways for this emerging profession are still evolving internationally. This study aimed to describe educational needs of practicing VSs and to develop a structured training program informed by those needs. A national survey was distributed to practicing VSs across Israeli clinical genetics centers to assess training background, learning, access to interpretation tools, and professional challenges. Survey findings informed the definition of core competencies and the development of a phased training program by a multidisciplinary working group. Thirty-eight respondents were included. Professional training was mostly acquired through observation of expert analysts (42.1%), followed by hands-on experience (39.5%). Only 18.4% participated in a dedicated VS course. Key challenges included keeping pace with evolving guidelines (55.3%) and copy number variant (CNV) analysis (47.4%). The survey identified substantial variability in training pathways and highlighted priority areas for structured education. Based on these findings, a structured training program was developed, combining theoretical modules, practical training, and assessment via a standardized proficiency test, supported by institutional forums and national meetings. This study presents a structured, scalable VS training program informed by a national needs assessment. By aligning the curriculum with identified educational needs, it provides a practical model that may support more standardized VS training and inform similar initiatives in clinical genomics internationally.

papers.title: Detection of common neonatal sepsis pathogens using a contemporary pediatric blood culture system.
papers.abstract: To evaluate recovery and time to positivity (TTP) of neonatal sepsis pathogens at low and ultra-low organism concentrations using a contemporary pediatric automated blood culture system. Six common neonatal sepsis pathogens were prepared in a 1:1 mixture of donor whole blood and saline-organism suspension at final concentrations ranging from ≤1 to 10-20 CFU/mL. Aliquots of 0.25-2.0 mL, containing 0.125-1.0 mL donor whole blood, were inoculated into BD BACTEC Peds Plus/F bottles. Recovery and TTP were assessed. Clinically important neonatal pathogens remained recoverable at very low inocula, including ≤1 CFU/mL. Median TTP ranged from 10 to 12 h for Escherichia coli and Streptococcus agalactiae to 20-26 h for coagulase-negative staphylococci. Increasing organism concentration shortened TTP for E. coli, Haemophilus influenzae, Staphylococcus capitis, and S. agalactiae. Inoculated suspension volume had relatively little effect on TTP among recovered cultures. Recovery improved across larger inoculated suspension volumes, particularly for staphylococcal organisms. A contemporary pediatric blood culture system demonstrated excellent recovery of common neonatal sepsis pathogens, including at very low organism concentrations. Larger inoculated suspension volumes primarily improved pathogen recovery rather than substantially faster detection. These findings support optimizing and documenting blood culture specimen volume as part of neonatal diagnostic stewardship. Common neonatal sepsis pathogens remained recoverable at very low organism concentrations, including ≤1 CFU/mL, using a contemporary pediatric blood culture system. Organism-specific differences in time to positivity were more pronounced than the generally modest effects of organism concentration or inoculated suspension volume. Larger inoculated suspension volumes primarily improved pathogen recovery rather than detection speed. Recovery of staphylococci was reduced at smaller inoculated suspension volumes, particularly at ultra-low organism concentrations. These findings support attention to specimen volume and documentation of the volume obtained as components of neonatal diagnostic and antimicrobial stewardship.

papers.title: PmiREN3.0: a multi-omics integrated and AI-assisted encyclopedia for plant microRNA research.
papers.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are key post-transcriptional regulators in gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Comprehensive research on miRNAs increasingly requires the integration of large and heterogeneous datasets, together with more efficient approaches to knowledge exploration. Here, we present PmiREN3.0, a major update of the Plant MicroRNA Encyclopedia. Compared with PmiREN2.0, species/subspecies coverage increased from 179 to 340, adding 22 orders, 51 families, and 108 genera. Using the same standardized workflow and annotation criteria as previous releases, high-confidence miRNAs were identified from 5319 small RNA sequencing (sRNA-seq) datasets, with miRNA loci increasing from 39 751 to 87 667 and miRNA families from 7838 to 18 389. Resources and tools from previous releases were extensively updated, while six new modules were added for primary transcripts, DNA methylation, RNA modifications, stress-responsive expression, metabolic pathways, and core GRNs. PmiREN3.0 also introduces miRai+, a knowledge service powered by artificial intelligence (AI) that combines a language model fine-tuned on miRNA knowledge with retrieval augmented generation. Evaluation yielded scores of 0.910 for answer relevance, 0.965 for faithfulness, and 0.906 for factual correctness. Together, PmiREN3.0 provides an expanded plant miRNA dataset and an integrated platform combining multi-omics data and AI-assisted knowledge services for plant miRNA research. PmiREN3.0 is available at https://pmiren.com/.

papers.title: Simpler is not always better: Phylodynamic misspecification and deep-learning corrections.
papers.abstract: Phylodynamics bridges the gap between epidemiology and pathogen genetic data. The birth-death (BD) model and its extensions serve to infer the average number of secondary infections Re and the infection duration d from time-scaled pathogen phylogenies. Moreover, more complex models add extra parameters, such as the average length of the incubation period, the proportion of superspreaders in the infected population, or the speed-up in detection after contact-tracing. However, these additional parameters come at an important computational cost: While the simplest, BD, model, has a closed-form solution, its extensions do not and require numerical methods for their likelihood computation. This leads to increased computational times and potential numerical errors. Therefore, the BD model remains the favorite researchers'choice for real dataset analyses, and is often applied even in cases where more complex epidemiological aspects are present. We investigated, using simulations, how model misspecification influences inference of Re and d in the phylodynamic framework. We showed that the use of models not accounting for various epidemiological aspects leads to bias. In particular the simplest, BD, estimator tends to underestimate Re in the presence of super-spreading, incubation or contact-tracing, which might be dangerous from the public health perspective. In contrast, deep-learning-based estimators for complex models, accounting for multiple epidemiological factors, performed well in our simulations both on the data where those factors were present and where they were absent. This motivates the use of complex epidemiologically realistic estimators, whose design has recently become possible thanks to deep learning.

papers.title: Cotton Cultivar Effects on DNA-Based Quantification of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. vasinfectum Race 4 in Soil.
papers.abstract: The soilborne fungal pathogen Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. vasinfectum race 4 (FOV4) poses a risk to U.S. cotton ( Gossypium spp.) following detection in California, Texas, and New Mexico. This study evaluated the influence of cotton cultivar resistance on relative variation in soil FOV4 DNA quantity, a proxy for inoculum density, in a naturally infested field over 2 years. Field trials included Upland ( G. hirsutum ) and Pima ( G. barbadense ) cotton cultivars and measured plant mortality, root necrosis, and lint yield. Bulk soil FOV4 DNA was quantified by qPCR at three timepoints each year: planting, midseason (first flower), and late season (crop maturity). Susceptible Pima cultivars exhibited the highest mortality, most severe necrosis, and lowest yields, whereas resistant Pima and Upland cultivars had lower necrosis with variable mortality and yield. Commercial Upland cultivars with differing degrees of susceptibility showed intermediate mortality and necrosis yet high yields. Midseason soil FOV4 DNA levels varied among cultivars in both years ( P = 0.011, 0.028), with elevated levels in a subset of susceptible cultivars. Late season DNA levels varied among cultivars in 2021 ( P = 0.017) but not in 2020 ( P = 0.080) and did not correspond to resistance designations. Within cultivars, mortality correlated with FOV4 DNA levels at planting ( P < 0.001, McFadden's pseudo- R 2 [ R 2 MF ] = 0.810) and late season ( P < 0.001, R 2 MF = 0.802), necrosis with late season DNA levels ( P < 0.001, R 2 = 0.849), and yield showed no correlation with FOV4 DNA at any timepoint. These findings relate host response to DNA-based soil pathogen quantification and emphasize resistance variation as a determinant of FOV4 disease ecology and management success.

papers.title: Auditory Evoked Potentials Differ from Controls and Correlate with Aspects of Cognition in Kabuki Syndrome and Rubinstein-Taybi Syndrome
papers.abstract: Objective Kabuki syndrome (KS) and Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome (RSTS) are two disorders caused by dysfunctional components of the epigenetic machinery and both result in intellectual disability. Mouse models of both KS and RSTS have seen reversal of cognitive impairment with epigenetic treatments. However, a great need exists for biomarkers in these disorders to improve the likelihood of successful clinical trials. This study aimed to investigate cortical auditory evoked potentials (AEPs) in KS and RSTS so that it could potentially be developed into a response biomarker in the future. Methods The amplitude of the N1-P2-N2 complex was measured for passive listening to monotonal auditory stimuli in individuals with KS, with RSTS, and typically developing controls. A standardized cognitive assessment battery was performed and specific subtests were correlated with AEP values. Results Groups differed significantly in P2, N2, and P2-N2 amplitude although RSTS was consistently more different from typically developing controls than was KS. The mid- to late-phase AEP components (P2 and N2) also correlate with cognition within and across these groups particularly with language whereas earlier components N1 and P2 correlate more with measures of executive functioning. Conclusion Late-phase components of AEPs differ in KS and RSTS from each other and from controls. KS and RSTS differ from controls in P2 and N2 amplitude in the same direction and both show a positive correlation between language and P2 amplitude and a negative correlation between language and N2 amplitude. Together they also show an association with N1 and P2 amplitude and executive functioning. Significance AEPs may turn out to be a valuable response biomarker in KS and RSTS individually and together.

papers.title: Endothelial protein C receptor is an entry receptor for Langya virus
papers.abstract: Langya virus (LayV) was recently discovered in infected individuals with febrile illness and classified as a Parahenipavirus, a group of poorly understood pathogens. LayV is distantly related to Nipah henipavirus which causes recurring outbreaks with case fatality rates reaching up to 90%. No vaccines or therapeutics are approved for use in humans for any parahenipavirus or henipavirus despite their broad geographic distribution and pandemic potential. Here, we discovered that human endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR) is an entry receptor for LayV and that the tetrameric LayV attachment glycoprotein (G) binds EPCR avidly. We reveal the molecular basis of LayV G recognition of the EPCR receptor and provide a blueprint of the determinants of receptor ortholog usage. We found that human and shrew EPCR orthologs promote cell entry of LayV and of the closely related Mojiang pseudoviruses. These results along with the detection of several Parahenipaviruses in shrews set these pathogens apart from Henipaviruses, which use Pteropid fruit bats as reservoir hosts. Our data support future surveillance efforts, by enabling prediction of EPCR utilization among newly discovered Parahenipaviruses, and the development and evaluation of countermeasures targeting this emerging group of human pathogens.

papers.title: RPFace: From biased structural benchmarks to generalizable RNA-protein interface prediction
papers.abstract: Modeling protein-RNA complexes with co-folding and docking methods is routine, yet these methods are evaluated on benchmarks whose composition mirrors the deposited structures on which they were trained or tuned, leaving open whether their reported performance reflects true generalization. Here, we focus the evaluation on the region that carries the biological signal: the binding interface. For the first time, we construct and release a fair benchmark that stratifies protein-RNA data into distinct structural and experimental groups, providing a more stringent test of generalization than aggregate averages. On this benchmark, we find that accuracy of detecting the binding site using co-folding methods is concentrated in ribosomal complexes and varies systematically with factors such as experimental modality. For docking methods, it is reliable only when the input conformations are already close to the bound state, and it is inconsistent across RNA classes. Both families of methods fail to transfer to in vivo CLIP experiments. To address this gap, we introduce RPFace, to the best of our knowledge the first model that jointly predicts the binding preference of every protein residue and every RNA nucleotide directly from sequence, requiring no experimental structure, template, or multiple sequence alignment. RPFace combines an ensemble of predicted secondary structures with a multi-modal embedding-enrichment scheme that fuses representations from RNA foundation models and structure prediction models. Unlike existing approaches, it is a very small and fast model that delivers stable performance across structural and experimental conditions, is robust to conformational change, and generalizes to in vivo datasets without extensive pretraining. As a result, RPFace matches the state-of-the-art methods on protein interfaces with no evolutionary information, and outperforms them on RNA interfaces, with the largest gains in zero-shot settings despite using only sequence information. The model, code, and data are available at Github.

papers.title: An expansive internal chemosensory system in the insect abdomen implicates Gustatory Receptors in diverse aspects of interoception
papers.abstract: Taste and olfactory receptors are gatekeepers that convey chemical information about the external environment. Their role in chemosensory systems has been extensively studied in several model system, which established their role in triggering discrete behavioral as well as physiological responses related to feeding and social interactions. Over time, cases of chemoreceptors expressed internally in organs not linked to the external chemosensory systems of taste and olfaction have been reported. Here, we present the existence of a complex internal chemosensory system in the abdomen of Drosophila melanogaster. We show that the adult fruit fly harbors a complex internal chemosensory system, composed of about 80 to 100 abdominal chemosensory neurons (ACSNs) expressing approximately 20 different Gustatory receptor (Gr) genes, including all sugar receptor and several members of the less conserved bitter receptor genes. The cells expressing specific Gr genes are stereotypically arranged along the entire circumference of the abdominal body wall, in proximity of muscle and fat layers. The ACSN fall into at least nine different subtypes based on co-expression analysis, projection trajectories into the Abdominal Ganglion (AG) and location of cell somata. Identification of different subpopulation of ASCNs expressing discrete combinations of Gr genes indicates that these receptor complexes have new, previously not considered roles in interoception, including monitoring of different nutrients, detection of cell metabolites and their byproducts and chemicals associated with pathogens.

papers.title: Towards an analytical framework for investigating the neurophysiological influence of social context in speech perception
papers.abstract: Social information plays an important role in everyday speech communication, yet existing neurophysiological approaches provide limited means of isolating its contribution during naturalistic speech perception. Here, we present an analytical framework that combines the large language model (LLM) Mistral-Instruct, fine-tuned on conversational language, and temporal response functions (TRFs) to investigate the influence of social context on word-level speech processing. The framework disentangles local context (LC) from speaker-specific social context (SC) when generating LLM-derived lexical expectation measures, enabling such predictions to be generated under either matching or mismatching speaker contexts for the same speech material. This provides a direct way of isolating the contribution of social information to lexical predictions. We first show that speaker-related social context carries information about speech register and conversational role beyond that available from previous local context alone by interrogating Mistral-Instruct. We then demonstrate that lexical expectations generated from socially congruent contexts produce small but reliable improvements in EEG prediction relative to expectations generated from incongruent social contexts. These effects were observed despite identical acoustic input and neural recordings, indicating that the influence of social context on lexical expectations explains dissociable variance in neural responses to speech. Together, these findings provide a proof of concept for using LLM-derived lexical expectations to isolate and measure the influence of social context on speech processing. More broadly, the proposed framework offers a flexible approach for generating and testing hypotheses about how different forms of contextual knowledge shape neural responses during naturalistic language comprehension.

papers.title: TailEnrich enables discovery of dysregulated genes through disease sample enrichment testing
papers.abstract: Identifying differentially expressed genes is fundamental to elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying complex diseases. However, in complex disorders such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), the genes exhibiting dysregulated expression may vary among patient subsets, reflecting the heterogeneity of the underlying pathological processes. Consequently, pathogenic genes are profoundly dysregulated in only a subset of patients. Conventional differential expression tools, such as DESeq2 and edgeR, are primarily designed to detect population-level expression shifts and may have limited power to identify subgroup-specific dysregulation. To overcome this limitation, we developed TailEnrich, a novel computational method that discovers dysregulated genes within patient subsets. TailEnrich independently tests the extreme left (downregulated) or right (upregulated) tails of a gene's expression distribution for disease sample enrichment. We quantify this enrichment using a new metric, i.e. the PE (Percentage of Enriched disease samples) score. On simulated datasets, TailEnrich demonstrates markedly improved accuracy over DESeq2 and edgeR in identifying dysregulated genes specific to patient subsets. Applied to AD gene expression data, TailEnrich uncovers a distinct, biologically relevant set of genes within key pathological pathways that are missed by mean shift-based approaches. TailEnrich provides a novel method for identifying dysregulated genes, and readily extends to other omics data including genomic variants and proteomics to uncover pathogenic genes in complex diseases.

papers.title: CauloBrowser 2.0: an AI powered update
papers.abstract: CauloBrowser is a systems-biology database for Caulobacter crescentus that organizes the largest repository of experimental data for this model bacterium. The original CauloBrowser provided a web interface for accessing these data, but the growing number of experimental datasets and advances in AI chatbots motivated an updated resource. We developed CauloBrowser 2.0 (CauloBrowser.org) as an open-source application that broadens access to RNA-seq, microarray, ribosome profiling, Tn-seq, ChIP-seq, and genome annotation data. The CauloChat AI interface allows users to query these datasets in natural language, generate visualizations, and achieve complex biological insights. While the database is hosted freely on the web, users may also download the database and run it locally, reducing dependence on the web-hosted service and allowing laboratories to use compatible unpublished datasets. Altogether, CauloBrowser 2.0 provides a significant update for exploring diverse systems biology data in C. crescentus.

papers.title: RadMultiBench: A Reproducible Dual-Task Benchmark Exposing the Limits of Pre-Trained Vision-Language Models Across Thoracic and Breast Imaging
papers.abstract: We present RadMultiBench, a multimodal benchmark of 6,148 medical images paired with expert radiological impressions across five categories--Breast Cancer, Lung Benign, Lung Malignant, Pneumonia, and Tuberculosis--targeting two core clinical tasks: automated report generation and disease classification. To enable reliable, repeatable experimentation, we provide a reproducible pipeline for data ingestion, de-identification, split management, and standardized reporting of text and classification metrics, facilitating dataset versioning and continuous benchmark testing. We compare three architectures: (1) a classical CNN-RNN with Bahdanau attention (ResNet-LSTM), (2) a general-domain vision-language (V-L) prefix-projection model (CLIP-GPT), and (3) a domain-specific V-L prefix-projection model (BioViL-T). Results reveal a sharp performance divide: the ResNet-LSTM attains near-perfect classification (99.5% accuracy) and is the only model to generate coherent reports (BLEU-4 = 0.021), whereas both prefix-projection models catastrophically fail generation (BLEU-4 [≤] 0.0001); moreover, the domain-specific BioViL-T also fails classification (11.5% accuracy). From a data-engineering angle, the pipeline is productionizable with lineage, feature registries, and continuous integration to guard against silent regressions when updating models or data; from a data-science angle, the benchmark provides baselines and analyses that foreground feature alignment and architectural suitability as first-order concerns, inviting ablations on multimodal objectives, retrieval-augmented encoders, and uncertainty-aware decoding. Overall, RadMultiBench highlights that state-of-the-art status in general V-L domains does not translate automatically to high-stakes clinical tasks, and it furnishes the tooling and evidence base needed to develop robust, clinically viable multimodal systems.

papers.title: pLM-bVAE: protein language model-enhanced binary representation improves quantum annealing-based protein sequence design
papers.abstract: Quantum annealing (QA) has been explored as an approach for protein design in vast combinatorial sequence spaces. Applying QA to protein sequence design requires amino acid sequences to be encoded as binary vectors, and optimized vectors to be decoded back into amino acid sequences. Thus, both the quality of binary encoding and sequence reconstruction accuracy are important for effective QA-based optimization. Binary variational autoencoder (bVAE) has been used to map protein sequences to binary representations in QA-based protein sequence design. However, bVAE was originally developed for natural language modeling, and its suitability for proteins has not been systematically evaluated. Here, we present pLM-bVAE, which incorporates protein representations derived from a pretrained protein language model (pLM) into the original bVAE model. In computational experiments on three public protein variant datasets, pLM-bVAE showed higher sequence reconstruction accuracy and binary encoding performance than bVAE. Moreover, we incorporated pLM-bVAE into a QA-based protein sequence design framework. Across all three datasets, pLM-bVAE generated more high-scoring sequences with greater sequence dissimilarity from the training and validation data than bVAE. Our results demonstrate that pLM-bVAE provides an effective binary representation for improving QA-based protein sequence design. Availability The source code used in this manuscript is available at https://github.com/hueda8/pLM-bVAE.

papers.title: Aging, HIV Status, and Sex Differentially Influence Antiretroviral Therapy Disposition Pathways in Rectosigmoid Tissue and Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells
papers.abstract: People living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) are increasingly surviving into older age due to the effectiveness of antiretroviral (ARV) therapy (ART), creating a growing population in whom age-related changes may influence treatment outcomes. Although aging is known to affect drug disposition, the molecular mechanisms by which aging alters ARV pharmacology remain incompletely understood, particularly within tissue compartments, including the rectosigmoid region of the colon, that serve as sites of HIV transmission and persistence. To address this knowledge gap, we used proteomics by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) to evaluate the impact of age and HIV status on proteins and pathways relevant to ARV disposition in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) and rectosigmoid colon tissue obtained from young (18-50) HIV-seronegative adults, older (65-80) HIV-seronegative adults, and older virally suppressed people living with HIV. We found that aging and HIV infection differentially influenced proteins predominantly within nucleos(t)ide reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) pathways, in rectosigmoid tissue and PBMC. HIV-associated effects to the proteome were more prominent in PBMC, whereas aging produced broader alterations in ARV disposition-related proteins in rectosigmoid tissue, including proteins involved in drug transport, intracellular drug activation, dephosphorylation, and nucleotide homeostasis. Several age-associated changes were further influenced by biologic sex, suggesting that aging may not affect ARV disposition uniformly across populations. To place these findings within a broader context, pathway analyses were performed that identified extensive tissue-specific remodeling associated with aging and HIV infection involving drug disposition, immune regulation, cellular metabolism, and disease-related pathways. Notably, aging was associated with alterations in pathways relevant to nucleotide metabolism and gastrointestinal tissue function, suggesting that processes beyond traditional drug transport and metabolism pathways may contribute to variability in ARV disposition with advancing age. Together, these findings identify aging as an important modifier of pathways that regulate ARV disposition within compartments relevant to HIV transmission and persistence. While the clinical consequences of our findings are unknown, these data provide a mechanistic foundation for future studies investigating whether age-associated changes influence the effectiveness of ART and HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis in older adults.

papers.title: Genome-wide Analysis of the VQ Gene Family and Expression Profiling in Sorghum bicolor
papers.abstract: Soil salinization severely restricts agricultural productivity, making the stress-tolerant sorghum an ideal model for studying crop adaptation. VQ motif-containing proteins are plant-specific transcriptional co-regulators vital for stress responses, yet their roles in sorghum remain underexplored. Here, we identified 35 VQ genes in sorghum, classifying them into seven subfamilies. Evolutionary analysis indicated that the family's expansion was primarily driven by segmental duplication. Notably, synteny analysis revealed a lack of collinearity between sorghum and Arabidopsis VQ genes, suggesting significant functional divergence during monocot evolution. Expression profiling showed distinct patterns among VQ members, with SbVQ34, SbVQ39 adn SbVQ40 significantly upregulated under salt stress. Furthermore, protein-protein interaction analysis highlighted SbVQ39 as a potential key regulator in sorghum salt tolerance. This study provides novel insights into sorghum's salinity tolerance mechanisms and establishes a foundation for utilizing VQ genes in breeding salt-tolerant crops.

papers.title: MAXWELL: Calibrating the probabilistic outputs of protein language models to the mutation-induced stability change landscape
papers.abstract: Designing mutations that enhance protein stability is a central goal in protein engineering. However, experimentally screening large numbers of candidate mutations is costly and time-consuming, creating a strong need for computational methods that can identify potentially stabilizing mutations. Among these approaches, protein language models are particularly promising because they learn context-dependent amino acid preferences from large-scale sequence and structure datasets. Nevertheless, most existing stability prediction methods use these models primarily as feature extractors and do not fully exploit the amino acid probability distributions they encode. Here, we introduce MAXWELL (Matrix-wise Landscape Learning), a novel post-training method that calibrates the probabilistic outputs learned by protein language models during pretraining to generate mutational landscapes that quantify the effects of individual amino acid substitutions on protein stability. When applied to ProteinMPNN, MAXWELL yields a state-of-the-art predictor of the effects of protein mutations on stability, outperforming ThermoMPNN and other representative methods on a curated benchmark of experimentally measured stability changes. We next applied MAXWELL to the design of ten single-point mutations in the DhaA dehalogenase, seven of which (70%) increased thermal stability. Among them, G171W showed the largest improvement, with a measured {Delta}T of 4.91 . These experimental results establish MAXWELL as a novel post-training strategy for protein language models and a practical framework for designing stabilizing mutations.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Protein-Ligand Binding Site Prediction from Protein Sequence and SMILES
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of protein-ligand binding sites is critical for mechanistic biology and drug discovery, yet predictive performance varies substantially across ligand families and data-availability regimes. We present a systematic ligand-aware benchmark and evaluation framework for residue-level binding-site prediction across three settings: overrepresented ligands with abundant examples, underrepresented ligands with limited examples, and zero-shot ligands unseen during training. Using a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering, we evaluate a progressive three-stage sequence-based modeling suite designed to study these regimes. Stage 1 trains ligand-specific predictors using a pretrained protein language model (PLM). Stage 2 introduces ligand conditioning through learned embeddings, enabling a single multi-ligand model. Stage 3 replaces these embeddings with representations from a pretrained chemical language model (CLM) operating on SMILES, enabling prediction for previously unseen ligands. In the original three-stage comparison, Stage 2 achieved a higher ligand-macro F1 than Stage 1 on the overrepresented test set (0.5832 versus 0.4769), although the comparison simultaneously changes predictor architecture, ligand conditioning, and the training regime. Stage 2 also outperformed several sequence- and structure-based baselines. Stage 3 achieves a pooled residue-level F1 of 0.3109 and a ligand-macro F1 of 0.2338 on previously unseen ligands, while remaining competitive on represented ligands. Control experiments using constant, mismatched, and scrambled SMILES inputs reduce performance across all three test regimes, providing evidence that the model uses information associated with the supplied ligand input rather than relying solely on generic protein binding-site propensity. Ablations across five PLM scales and multiple CLMs further show that increasing PLM scale generally improves performance, although the trend is not strictly monotonic, whereas CLM scaling produces smaller and less consistent gains. Overall, this study provides a systematic benchmark for quantifying the effect of ligand data availability on residue-level binding-site prediction and for evaluating generalization to previously unseen ligands.

papers.title: Molecular Characterization of T-Lineage Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia by an Optimal-Transport Based Multi-Omics Integration Framework
papers.abstract: T-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) is an aggressive pediatric malignancy characterized by complex heterogeneity across multiple molecular layers. Accurate subtyping is essential for understanding disease mechanisms, risk stratification, and guiding targeted therapeutic strategies. However, current diagnostic approaches are labor-intensive and time-consuming, and existing computational methods are limited by reliance on single-modality data or simple integration strategies. Effective integration of heterogeneous multi-omics data remains a major computational challenge. We present OTTER (Optimal Transport-based Transcriptomics and gEnomics Representation), a novel multi-modal deep learning framework that jointly models transcriptomic and genomic data for T-ALL molecular characterization. OTTER encodes each omics modality through a modality-specific encoder and aligns the resulting latent representations using Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport (GW-OT), which preserves the internal geometric structure of each modality without requiring a shared feature space. Benchmarking tests on the Children's Oncology Group (COG) AALL0434 cohort with >1,300 patients across 17 T-ALL subtypes suggested that OTTER significantly outperformed state-of-the-art approaches for T-ALL molecular characterization. In addition, OTTER could identify interpretable subtype-defining and omics-specific features for T-ALL. Furthermore, we have demonstrated the generalizability of OTTER by evaluating on multiple external independent clinical cohorts. In summary, OTTER provides a principled, biologically interpretable, and computationally effective framework for multi-omics driven T-ALL molecular characterization and broader cancer applications.

papers.title: Multi-agent LLM teams improve differential recall on curated cases but underperform on emergency working-label matching: a two-cohort, two-family evaluation
papers.abstract: Background. Whether multi-agent large language model (LLM) pipelines help, add nothing, or underperform a single call may depend on the input and scoring contract rather than the architecture; these boundary conditions are unmapped. Methods. We compared a single direct call (Ax1), five personas in one context (P), and five isolated roles integrated by a moderator (MDT) across curated corpora (87 clinicopathological cases, 406 MedCaseReasoning cases, 392 replication vignettes) and two disjoint emergency cohorts from one repository (364 mixed-label encounters; a protocol-frozen 400-encounter disease-label-only replacement, one local serving stack). Scoring was judge-mediated top-k working-label matching. A completed factorial isolated the active ingredient; a symptom-permissive output-contract arm tested contract fit; three physicians rated discordant cases. Findings. On curated corpora MDT improved differential-list recall (top-3: +5.5 points, p = 0.0079; +3.0, p = 0.0079; +3.3, p = 0.0013) but not top-1 accuracy; the factorial attributed the gain to independent generation plus moderated synthesis, not personas. On emergency presentations the sign reversed: in the disease-label-only cohort Ax1 led MDT at every endpoint (top-3 -5.2 points, 95% CI -8.0 to -2.4, p = 0.0008), a second family reproduced it, and bridged cases excluded the serving stack. A symptom-permissive contract shrank the deficit's point estimates by 52-75%, replacement-cohort intervals all spanning zero though remaining negative; the clause harmed no arm.
